memory_update.text: BNED should remain the primary direct underfollowed candidate for the campus bookstore/course-material access node; it has direct inclusive-access exposure and a disclosed 45% related-party supplier concentration in FY2025.
WLY is a mid-cap second-order supplier candidate because its Learning segment includes academic courseware, inclusive access, and STEM digital courseware exposure.

NNI is a second-order campus-commerce infrastructure candidate; the key unresolved question is whether its payment/online-storefront workflows directly process course-material or inclusive-access charges.
Publisher power remains central to the node: Pearson and Wiley help frame how digital courseware and inclusive-access licensing terms may pressure or reinforce campus-store distributors.

Private assets such as Follett, McGraw Hill, Cengage, and Ingram/VitalSource appear highly relevant but are not US-listed common-equity candidates; future passes should map them as private counterparties/suppliers rather than public candidates.

node: Campus bookstore, course-material access, and publisher-distribution layer
summary: Expanded the US-listed universe around the course-material distribution node using a two-lane Serenity funnel. The clearest underfollowed asset is Barnes & Noble Education, a small-cap campus bookstore/course-material operator with direct exposure to inclusive-access programs and material supplier concentration. Second-order candidates include Wiley as a mid-cap academic publisher/courseware supplier and Nelnet as a mid-cap campus-commerce/payment infrastructure provider adjacent to student billing and online storefront workflows. Pearson is included as a reference/context anchor because it is a large courseware publisher and inclusive-access participant, but it is above the preferred underfollowed market-cap range.
